use: Tells someone you don't mind which; add yo to sound easygoing rather than bored.

example.romaji: ramen demo sushi demo, dotchi demo ii yo.
example.ja: ラーメンでも寿司でも、どっちでもいいよ。
example.english: Ramen or sushi, either's fine with me.

examplePolite.romaji: watashi wa dochira demo ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 私はどちらでもいいですよ。

notes: Said flatly it can sound like you don't care. Nan demo ii means anything is fine.

english: could you do that for me?; could I ask for...?
use: Polite request to staff, colleagues or strangers, after naming the thing or task.

example.romaji: kore, kopii onegai dekimasu ka?
example.ja: これ、コピーお願いできますか？
example.english: Could you make a copy of this for me?

politeJa: ちょっと手伝ってもらえますか
english: give me a hand for a sec
use: Quick call for help to family, friends or a close coworker.

example.romaji: chotto tetsudatte! kore omoi.
example.ja: ちょっと手伝って！これ重い。
example.english: Give me a hand! This is heavy.

examplePolite.ja: すみません、ちょっと手伝ってもらえますか？
examplePolite.english: Sorry, could you give me a hand?

notes: Add kureru? to soften it: chotto tetsudatte kureru?

use: Warmly lets someone go first, sit down or take something; doubling it makes it eager.

example.romaji: douzo douzo, saki ni haitte.
example.ja: どうぞどうぞ、先に入って。
example.english: Go ahead, you go in first.

examplePolite.romaji: douzo douzo, saki ni haitte kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: どうぞどうぞ、先に入ってください。

notes: A single douzo is the everyday here you go when handing something over.

politeJa: 気を使わないでください
english: don't go to any trouble; you didn't have to
use: Said when someone fusses over you or brings a gift; it's polite modesty, so still accept with thanks.

example.romaji: sonna ni ki o tsukawanaide yo.
example.ja: そんなに気を使わないでよ。
example.english: Oh, you didn't need to go to all that trouble.

examplePolite.ja: どうぞ気を使わないでください。
examplePolite.english: Please don't go to any trouble.

notes: Formal set version: douzo okizukai naku. Ki o tsukau means to be considerate or fuss over someone.

politeJa: お茶でもいかがですか
english: how about a tea or something?; want to grab a coffee?
use: Low-pressure invitation to sit and chat over a drink, at home or at a cafe.

example.romaji: jikan aru nara, ocha demo dou?
example.ja: 時間あるなら、お茶でもどう？
example.english: If you've got time, how about a coffee?

examplePolite.romaji: yokattara, ocha demo ikaga desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: よかったら、お茶でもいかがですか？
examplePolite.english: If you like, would you care for some tea?

notes: Ocha suru means stopping at a cafe, not only drinking tea.

src: お願いがあるんだけど
ja: お願いがあるんだけど
kana: おねがいがあるんだけど
romaji: onegai ga aru n da kedo
polite: onegai ga aru n desu ga
politeJa: お願いがあるんですが
english: I have a favour to ask
use: Opens a bigger favour; the other person usually answers nani? and then you explain.

example.romaji: nee, chotto onegai ga aru n da kedo.
example.ja: ねえ、ちょっとお願いがあるんだけど。
example.english: Hey, I've got a favour to ask.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, onegai ga aru n desu ga.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、お願いがあるんですが。
examplePolite.english: Excuse me, I have a favour to ask.

use: Ask staff in shops, restaurants and stations; casual is toire doko?

example.romaji: sumimasen, toire wa doko desu ka?
example.ja: すみません、トイレはどこですか？
example.english: Excuse me, where's the toilet?

notes: Otearai is a politer word for toilet. At someone's home: toire karite mo ii desu ka?

src: 何かあったら言ってね
ja: 何かあったら言ってね
kana: なにかあったらいってね
politeJa: 何かあったら言ってください
english: let me know if you need anything
use: Friendly offer of ongoing help, said when leaving someone to get on with things.

example.romaji: nanika attara itsu demo itte ne.
example.ja: 何かあったらいつでも言ってね。
example.english: If you need anything, just say so, anytime.

examplePolite.romaji: nanika attara itsu demo itte kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: 何かあったらいつでも言ってくださいね。
examplePolite.english: Please let me know anytime if you need anything.

notes: Literally if anything happens, tell me, so it's also said to someone sick or worried.

use: Turns down an invitation by trailing off; the unfinished sentence is the polite no, so no long excuse is needed.

example.romaji: gomen, kyou wa chotto... ashita nara ii yo.
example.ja: ごめん、今日はちょっと…明日ならいいよ。
example.english: Sorry, today's not great... tomorrow works, though.

examplePolite.ja: すみません、今日はちょっと…

notes: Chotto... alone works for any request you'd rather refuse.

politeJa: じゃあそれでお願いします
use: Settles a plan or choice someone just suggested; to staff add onegai shimasu.

example.romaji: rokuji ni eki? un, jaa sore de.
example.ja: 6時に駅？うん、じゃあそれで。
example.english: Six at the station? Okay, let's go with that.

examplePolite.ja: じゃあ、それでお願いします。
examplePolite.english: Okay, I'll go with that, please.

english: help yourself if you like; please have some
use: Offers food, a seat or a spare item without pressure, e.g. passing snacks round at work; answer arigatou, itadakimasu.

example.romaji: okashi katte kita kara, yokattara douzo.
example.ja: お菓子買ってきたから、よかったらどうぞ。
example.english: I bought some snacks, help yourselves.

examplePolite.ja: お土産です。よかったらどうぞ。
examplePolite.english: It's a little souvenir. Please have some.

use: Tells a taxi driver to stop, or tells someone walking or driving you that they needn't go further.

example.romaji: a, koko de ii desu. arigatou gozaimasu.
example.ja: あ、ここでいいです。ありがとうございます。
example.english: Oh, here's fine. Thank you.

notes: Clearer to a taxi driver: koko de tomete kudasai (please stop here).

politeJa: じゃあ遠慮なくいただきます
english: well, don't mind if I do
use: Accepts food, drink or a gift after a show of hesitation.

example.romaji: ii no? jaa, enryo naku!
example.ja: いいの？じゃあ、遠慮なく！
example.english: Really? Well, don't mind if I do!

examplePolite.ja: では、遠慮なくいただきます。

notes: The host often says enryo shinaide (don't hold back) first.

kana: えんりょしておきます
use: Polite no to an offer or invitation, softer than kekkou desu.

example.romaji: kyou wa enryo shite okimasu. mata sasotte kudasai.
example.ja: 今日は遠慮しておきます。また誘ってください。
example.english: I'll pass today. Please ask me again.

notes: Casual version: enryo shitoku. Enryo means holding back.

use: Answer to a shop assistant who asks if you're looking for something.

example.romaji: a, daijoubu desu. miteru dake desu.
example.ja: あ、大丈夫です。見てるだけです。
example.english: Oh, I'm fine. Just looking.

notes: Also means I'm only watching when someone asks you to join in.

use: Point at or name the item first: kore, ikura desu ka?

example.romaji: sumimasen, kore ikura desu ka?
example.ja: すみません、これいくらですか？
example.english: Excuse me, how much is this?

notes: Casual version: ikura? Prices come back as numbers plus en: sen en is 1,000 yen.

kana: りょうしゅうしょおねがいします
use: Asks for a formal receipt for expenses at shops, restaurants and taxis; staff may then ask what name to write.

example.romaji: sumimasen, ryoushuusho onegai shimasu.
example.ja: すみません、領収書お願いします。
example.english: Excuse me, could I get a receipt?

notes: A reshiito is the printed till slip; a ryoushuusho is the formal one for claiming expenses.

use: Polite way to leave a shop or counter without buying now.

example.romaji: sumimasen, ato de mata kimasu.
example.ja: すみません、あとでまた来ます。
example.english: Sorry, I'll come back later.

english: I'll take this one; I'll have this
use: Tells staff your choice after looking or comparing; works for food orders too.

example.romaji: jaa, kore ni shimasu.
example.ja: じゃあ、これにします。
example.english: Okay, I'll go with this one.

notes: X ni suru means decide on X. Casual version: kore ni suru.
